function.name: resolve
function.description: Find which client or task a spoken name refers to. Call this before any tool that takes an id. Returns a verdict of unique, ambiguous or none, with ranked candidates. Only act on unique; otherwise ask the user which they meant.

phrase.description: what the user said, for example 'northgate roof'

kind.description: omit this to search both clients and tasks

function.name: create_task
function.description: Create a new matter for an existing client. Only call this after the user has confirmed the matter does not already exist. client_id must come from resolve.

name.description: the matter name, for example 'Lease review'

function.name: log_time
function.description: Record time worked on a task. task_id must come from resolve or create_task.

seconds.description: duration in seconds; convert 'an hour and a half' to 5400 yourself

note.description: optional short note about the work

function.name: start_timer
function.description: Start a running timer on a task. task_id must come from resolve or create_task. Use this for 'start timing', not log_time.

function.name: stop_timer
function.description: Stop a running timer and record what it measured. This is the only way to stop a timer. Omit task_id to stop whatever is running, which is usually what 'stop that timer' means.

task_id.description: omit to stop every running timer

function.name: review_day
function.description: List everything recorded on one day, with the interval id of each entry. Call this before correcting or deleting, because it is where interval ids come from.

function.name: set_interval_duration
function.description: Change how long a recorded entry was, keeping its start time. interval_id must come from review_day or log_time.

function.name: delete_interval
function.description: Permanently remove a recorded entry. This cannot be undone. Not for stopping a timer, use stop_timer for that. Only call it when the user asked to delete this specific entry and said yes after you described it. Both ids must come from review_day.

function.name: list_tasks
function.description: Every matter being tracked, with its total time. Omit client_id for all clients. Use this when the user asks what exists, or when resolve finds nothing and you need to see what is actually there. Use review_day instead for what happened on a particular day.

client_id.description: omit to list every client's matters

function.name: create_client
function.description: Add a new client. Only after the user has confirmed the client does not already exist -- check with list_tasks or resolve first.

function.name: check_rules
function.description: Read the client's Outside Counsel Guidelines for one matter and report what they say about the proposed work. Returns a finding, a summary to read out, the section it came from, and any fields still missing. This is the only source of a citation -- never state a section number that did not come from here.

category.description: timekeeper_attendance for who may work on or attend something; expert_retention for engaging an expert, consultant or vendor; travel_time for billing travel; expense_threshold for a disbursement

person.description: the timekeeper or the expert, when the question is about one

hours.description: estimated hours, if the lawyer gave one

amount_dollars.description: estimated cost in dollars, if the lawyer gave one

days_ahead.description: 0 for today, 1 for tomorrow. An approval only counts if it was decided before the work.

function.name: draft_approval
function.description: Write an approval request for work that check_rules said needs one. Call it only after the lawyer says yes. Pass the same arguments you passed to check_rules. Returns the recipient, subject and body. Nothing is sent -- say so.

category.description: the same category you passed to check_rules

person.description: the timekeeper or expert the request is about
